_meta.description: Live macro themes affecting currencies but not on the scheduled news calendar. Update as regime-changing events happen. Scanner reads this at brief generation time and displays it in the daily/weekly review.
_meta.howToUse: Each theme should include: (1) short title, (2) start date, (3) currency implications with brief reasoning, (4) a specific watchLevel that would invalidate the theme, (5) affectedPairs for scanner correlation. Retire themes by moving to _retired[] with an endDate.
_meta.maintenance: Manual updates + Claude WebSearch each session. 2026-09-23 refresh: WTI crude extending losses for sixth consecutive session to ~$91.30-93.82 range (Sep 23) as Trump describes US-Iran talks as 'very good' and Hormuz traffic proves resilient — oil down ~12% from $106 peak, removing CAD buffer and easing Dec-hike inflation fears at the margin; DXY at ~100.6, near highest since late July; FOMC Oct 27-28 now a live binary with ~54% hike probability priced per futures (upgraded from hold expectation); Dec hike still ~66% priced; BOJ Oct 29-30 unchanged at high hike odds; BoC Oct 28 unchanged. Three active themes maintained; no retirements; post-dual-hike-divergence upgraded to reflect Oct FOMC as live binary alongside Dec.

themes.title: Canada-US trade war live — Sep 8 retaliation in effect, Trump federal-contracts ban, oil now at ~$92 deepening USDCAD upside; Jan 1 2027 50% auto tariff threat structural; BoC Oct 28 next binary
themes.summary: As of September 23, the Canada-US trade war remains structurally unchanged with all tariff escalations intact and zero diplomatic off-ramp visible, while the critical oil variable has now deteriorated sharply in a CAD-negative direction. Canada's C$27.6 billion retaliatory package (15%, 25%, and 50% tariff rates across 700+ US goods lines, doubling steel and aluminum duties to 50%) has been live since 12:01 a.m. September 8. Trump's federal-contracts ban on Canadian-origin products remains unrevoked. The commodity situation has deteriorated materially since the Sep 21 update: WTI crude has now fallen for six consecutive sessions, declining from the mid-week peak near $106 to today's Sep 23 range of approximately $91.30-93.82 — a drop of roughly $12-14 from peak. The catalyst for the extended oil decline is US-Iran diplomatic progress: President Trump described a meeting between US officials and Iranian envoys as 'very good,' and satellite data showed Hormuz tanker traffic proving more resilient than feared, with Saudi Arabia moving crude through the Strait at approximately 2.9 million barrels per day over the past six days. The sustained fall in WTI toward the $91-94 range is now a significant CAD headwind: the primary commodity offset that had been capping USDCAD below 1.3900 has been removed, and the net directional bias is now clearly USDCAD bullish from both the tariff-war fundamental and the oil-collapse channels simultaneously. Canadian August employment printed -41,700 (vs +15,000 expected), confirming ongoing labor market damage from the tariff conflict. The Bank of Canada next meets October 28 — a stagflationary dilemma (deteriorating labor, tariff-driven inflation pass-through) that could produce a dovish surprise cut, providing a third USDCAD upside driver. The FOMC September 16 hike to 3.75-4.00% (12-0 confirmed) and now approximately 54% market-implied probability of an October 27-28 FOMC hike add compounding USD tailwinds to USDCAD that were not priced during the prior week. The structural Jan 1, 2027 threat of 50% tariffs on all Canadian autos, trucks, parts, and steel remains the medium-term CAD overhang. No diplomatic off-ramp is visible.

implications.CAD: MAXIMUM structural CAD negative from tariff war — US Section 338 50% tariffs live since Aug 22, Canada 700+ line retaliation live since Sep 8, Trump federal-contracts ban unrevoked, zero diplomatic off-ramp, Jan 1 2027 50% auto tariff threat. Oil CAD tailwind has now collapsed: WTI down six consecutive sessions from ~$106 peak to ~$91-94 on Sep 23 as US-Iran diplomacy advances and Hormuz proves resilient — the primary USDCAD cap is gone. Net directional bias is now clearly USDCAD bullish from both tariff fundamentals and oil decline. BoC Oct 28 binary: stagflationary dilemma (labor -41,700 Aug, tariff inflation pass-through) — dovish cut accelerates CAD weakness toward 1.4100; hawkish hold provides brief relief toward 1.3800.
implications.USD: FOMC confirmed 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16 (12-0 unanimous). Futures now pricing ~54% probability of another 25bp at Oct 27-28 FOMC. Dot plot year-end median 4.1% implies at least one more hike. USD broadly supported by Warsh tightening cycle. USDCAD directionally bullish on triple drivers: tariff war fundamentals, USD rate advantage, and oil collapse removing the CAD offset.
implications.MXN: USMCA credibility damage from US-Canada rupture keeps uncertainty elevated for Mexico. US-Mexico bilateral divergence from US-Canada adds structural MXN uncertainty premium.
implications.EUR: Indirect — EURCAD likely bid on structural CAD weakness. Broader protectionism signal from Section 338 invocation has limited but non-zero EUR contagion via global trade uncertainty.
implications.AUD: Commodity-bloc — WTI collapse from $106 to $91-94 is a direct AUD headwind at the margin via risk-off and commodity complex repricing. Copper and iron ore dynamics dominate AUDUSD more directly but sustained oil weakness can drag broader commodity sentiment. Subject to tariff-war risk-off and USD strength from post-FOMC hike regime.
implications.NZD: Same as AUD. NZDCAD vol elevated. NZD defensive in commodity-bloc risk-off episodes.
implications.GBP: GBPCAD directional trade on CAD structural weakness. GBP otherwise dominated by BoE path.
implications.JPY: CADJPY under dual pressure — CAD structural weakness from Section 338 tariff war plus JPY structural bid from BOJ normalization cycle now confirmed at 1.25% with Oct 29-30 next binary at high hike odds.

themes.watchLevel: USDCAD — oil collapse to $91-94 range (Sep 23) from $106 peak has definitively removed the primary USDCAD cap. Key upside: 1.3900 resistance — clean daily close above 1.3900 opens 1.4017-1.4100 if oil stays below $97 and BoC Oct 28 is dovish. Key support: 1.3783 (Sep 8 low); sustained break below 1.3750 would require a dramatic oil re-escalation back above $103+. Oil re-escalation above $100 (US-Iran talks collapse, fresh Hormuz closure) = USDCAD partially capped again below 1.3900; oil falling toward $85 = USDCAD accelerates toward 1.41+. BoC Oct 28 binary: dovish cut = USDCAD toward 1.4100; hawkish hold = USDCAD relief to 1.3800. Theme ends only on: (1) formal re-opening of US-Canada talks with credible framework, or (2) Trump executive action suspending Section 338.

themes.title: BOJ hiked to 1.25% Sep 18 (7-2) but Ueda non-committal — USDJPY holding above 157; Oct 29-30 BOJ next binary at high hike odds; intervention regime at 160.00 intact; post-hike USD-JPY rate gap dominant
themes.summary: As of September 23, the post-BOJ September 18 dynamic is unchanged and consolidating: USDJPY is holding above 157 following the paradoxically dovish market reaction to the 7-2 vote hike to 1.25%. Governor Ueda's non-committal press conference — in which he offered no forward guidance on further hikes — caused USDJPY to push back above 157 despite the rate increase, a classic 'sell the fact' JPY dynamic. OCBC analysts note that the 7-2 vote split 'may remain a near-term headwind for the JPY,' but stress that 'the more important takeaway is that the BoJ appears increasingly willing to tighten policy at a faster pace.' The BOJ lifted its overnight call rate to 1.25% — the highest since 1995 and the sixth rate increase since exiting NIRP in March 2024. The dominant near-term drivers remain: (1) the persistent US-Japan rate differential — with the Fed at 3.75-4.00% (and ~54% market odds of an Oct 27-28 hike to 4.25%) versus BOJ at 1.25% — a gap of at least 250bp that keeps carry trade structurally attractive and USDJPY supported above 157; and (2) the BOJ October 29-30 meeting, which carries high market-implied hike odds per TONA futures, with a fresh Outlook Report due. Critically, the Oct 27-28 FOMC and Oct 29-30 BOJ meetings fall within 48 hours of each other, creating a dual binary window at end-October that could generate exceptional USDJPY volatility in either direction. The next policy-relevant data inputs are Japanese wage figures, the Tokyo CPI print, and US PCE/CPI data ahead of Oct 27-30 meeting window. The MoF/BOJ coordinated intervention regime at 160.00 remains fully intact. Fed's Collins delivered notably hawkish remarks post-Sep 16 hike (FXS Speechtracker 8.1/10 vs 6.6/10 baseline), reinforcing the USD side of the rate gap. Oil declining toward $91-94 provides minor USD safe-haven relief and slightly reduces yen-haven demand, mildly supportive of USDJPY staying elevated near current levels.

implications.JPY: BOJ hiked to 1.25% (7-2) but Ueda's non-committal presser caused USDJPY to push back above 157. The rate gap with the US (3.75-4.00% vs 1.25% = 250bp minimum, widening if Oct FOMC hikes) remains the dominant USDJPY driver and keeps carry trade structurally attractive. End-October dual binary: Oct 27-28 FOMC (~54% hike odds) followed immediately by Oct 29-30 BOJ (high hike odds with Outlook Report) creates an exceptional two-day vol event. Hawkish Outlook Report + BOJ 25bp hike = USDJPY drops toward 153-155; dovish BOJ hold or cautious guidance = USDJPY rally toward 159-160 and intervention risk maximally tested. JGB 10-year yield dipped on Ueda dovish read — watch for reversal as Oct hike odds stay elevated.
implications.USD: FOMC at 3.75-4.00% (Sep 16, 12-0) and futures now pricing ~54% Oct hike means the USD-JPY rate differential could widen further from the US side if Oct FOMC delivers. DXY at ~100.6 near highest since late July. Fed's Collins hawkish post-hike speeches reinforce USD rate advantage.
implications.EUR: EURJPY under dual pressure — BOJ normalization cycle intact at 1.25% with Oct 29-30 next hike at high odds vs ECB on hold. JGB yields structurally rising. Medium-term EUR-JPY rate differential narrowing.
implications.GBP: GBPJPY — Sep 18 BOJ hike delivered but dovish read limits near-term JPY upside. End-October dual binary (FOMC Oct 27-28 + BOJ Oct 29-30) is the next directional catalyst for JPY crosses.
implications.CHF: CHFJPY under BOJ normalization pressure. SNB in easing mode adds divergence — CHFJPY structurally lower over medium term.
implications.CAD: CADJPY under dual pressure — CAD structural weakness from Section 338 tariff war plus JPY structural bid from BOJ normalization cycle (1.25% delivered, Oct 29-30 at high hike odds).
implications.AUD: AUDJPY — Sep 18 BOJ hike delivered but Ueda dovish presser provided near-term relief. End-October dual binary (FOMC + BOJ within 48 hours) is the primary AUDJPY volatility catalyst. Oil decline to $91-94 mildly negative for AUD commodity bid.
implications.NZD: Same dynamic as AUD. NZDJPY under BOJ normalization structural pressure. End-October dual binary dominant catalyst.

themes.watchLevel: USDJPY ~157+ as of Sep 23 — holding above 157 on Ueda's non-committal presser post-Sep 18 hike and persistent rate gap. Key resistance: 158.50 (psychological); 160.00 is the hard intervention ceiling — MoF/BOJ coordinated intervention remains on record. Key support: 156.50; 155.00 (major round number); 153.00 (post-BOJ hike downside target if Oct 29-30 Outlook Report is hawkish). Critical end-October dual binary window: Oct 27-28 FOMC (~54% hike probability, would push Fed to 4.25%) followed immediately by Oct 29-30 BOJ (high hike odds with Outlook Report). Combined hawkish FOMC + dovish BOJ surprise = USDJPY rally toward 159-160 and intervention regime maximally tested; hawkish BOJ Outlook + dovish FOMC surprise = USDJPY drops toward 153. Watch Tokyo CPI, Japanese wage data, and US PCE/CPI as the primary pre-meeting signals. Theme invalidated: USDJPY sustained above 160.00 with MoF disclaimer = intervention regime broken; USDJPY below 150.00 = structural JPY bull trend in new leg requiring theme re-characterization.

themes.title: Post-dual-hike regime: Fed at 4.00% with Oct 27-28 FOMC now live (~54% hike odds) and Dec hike also priced; DXY at ~100.6 near July highs; oil collapse to $91-94 easing inflation tail risk; G10 rate divergence dominant
themes.summary: As of September 23, the post-FOMC regime is actively evolving in a more hawkish direction than anticipated at the Sep 21 update. The DXY is at approximately 100.6 on September 23, near its highest level since late July, as hawkish Federal Reserve commentary reinforces tightening expectations. The most significant development since Sep 21 is that the October 27-28 FOMC meeting has been upgraded to a live binary: futures markets are now pricing approximately 54% probability of a 25bp hike at October 27-28, which would bring the fed funds rate to 4.00-4.25% — and this October meeting falls just one day before the BOJ October 29-30 binary, creating an exceptional compounded vol event at end-October. Beyond October, futures are pricing an increase to approximately 4.2% by December and roughly 4.7% by September 2027, extending expectations for prolonged restrictive policy. The September dot plot showed a median projection of 4.1% at end-2026, consistent with one more hike (either October or December). Chair Warsh estimated August headline PCE near 3.6% and core PCE near 3.2%, with too many categories still rising above 3% — underpinning the tightening bias. Fed's Collins delivered hawkish post-hike remarks scoring 8.1/10 on the FXS Speechtracker versus a 6.6/10 baseline. An important countervailing development is the sharp oil decline: WTI has fallen for six consecutive sessions from a ~$106 peak to approximately $91.30-93.82 on September 23, driven by US-Iran diplomatic progress (Trump describing talks as 'very good') and evidence that Saudi Arabia is moving crude through Hormuz at approximately 2.9 million barrels per day. This oil decline has a dual effect on the post-hike divergence theme — it slightly reduces the upside inflation pressure that justified aggressive Fed hike pricing (a mild USD headwind at the margin) while simultaneously removing CAD's primary commodity offset (a USDCAD tailwind via the Canada theme). Net impact on DXY: broadly neutral to slightly positive as lower oil eases stagflation fears and improves real household income, supporting the 'soft landing' growth narrative that keeps the Fed hiking without triggering recession signals. EURUSD remains under pressure, with immediate support at 1.1360 and a break below that opening 1.1240. The G10 rate divergence map: Fed at 3.75-4.00% (hiking) vs ECB (hold), RBA (hold), RBNZ (hold), SNB (easing) creates structural USD strength across all non-JPY G10 pairs.

implications.USD: Broadly bullish. DXY at ~100.6 near highest since late July. Fed at 3.75-4.00% (Sep 16, 12-0), Oct 27-28 FOMC now live at ~54% hike odds, futures pricing ~4.2% by December and ~4.7% by Sep 2027. Warsh tightening cycle in full institutional execution. Next key levels: DXY 101-102 if Oct hike confirmed; 10yr UST sustained above 4.85% = confirmation of Dec hike fully priced. Oil decline to $91-94 is minor USD negative at the margin (eases inflation urgency) but does not materially alter the hawkish path.
implications.EUR: EURUSD bearish — ECB on hold while Fed hiking cycle has now added an Oct binary. EURUSD immediate support at 1.1360; break opens 1.1240; sustained break below 1.1240 targets 1.1100. Rate differential widening structurally USD-positive vs EUR. ECB Oct meeting could provide temporary EUR relief if hawkish surprise.
implications.GBP: GBPUSD under pressure from Fed-BoE divergence. BoE has its own inflation dynamics but Fed rate advantage is structurally USD-positive. GBPUSD below 1.3400 is next key target if Oct or Dec Fed hike fully priced.
implications.JPY: USDJPY above 157 — Fed at 4.00% (potentially 4.25% after Oct 27-28) vs BOJ at 1.25% is a 250-300bp rate gap that keeps carry trade structurally attractive. End-October is the critical dual binary (FOMC Oct 27-28 + BOJ Oct 29-30 within 48 hours). USDJPY upside capped by intervention at 160.00.
implications.CAD: USDCAD bullish from triple drivers — tariff war fundamentals, USD rate advantage from Fed at 4.00% with Oct/Dec hikes priced, and oil collapse to $91-94 removing the primary CAD commodity buffer. BoC Oct 28 policy binary adds fourth driver.
implications.AUD: AUDUSD bearish — RBA on hold while Fed hiking. AUDUSD retreating on rate differential headwind. Oil/commodity complex decline adds to AUD pressure. AUDUSD bias toward 0.68-0.69 area.
implications.NZD: NZDUSD bearish — RBNZ rate path less hawkish than Fed. Same dynamic as AUD. NZDUSD toward 0.5800 area on Oct/Dec hike pricing.
implications.CHF: USDCHF bullish — SNB in easing mode while Fed at 4.00% hiking. Oil decline reduces safe-haven CHF demand, adding to USDCHF upside. Rate divergence is structurally USDCHF positive.

themes.watchLevel: DXY at ~100.6 and 10yr UST are the daily signals. DXY: 101-102 is next target if Oct 27-28 FOMC hike confirmed; pullback below 99.50 = Oct hike doubts and USD gives back gains. 10yr UST: sustained above 4.85% = Oct+Dec hike fully priced; pullback below 4.60% = hike doubt. EURUSD: 1.1360 is immediate support; break opens 1.1240; bounce above 1.1450 = Oct hike doubt/risk-off. Critical data calendar now upgraded: October 27-28 FOMC is a live binary (~54% hike odds) — a delivered Oct hike front-runs December and accelerates DXY toward 101-102; a hold at Oct reinforces December as the last binary. US September PCE (early Oct), September CPI (mid-Oct), and October payrolls (early Nov) are the key inputs. Oil wildcard: WTI recovering above $100 (US-Iran talks collapse, Hormuz closure) = inflation urgency returns, Dec hike stays firmly priced AND adds AUD/CAD commodity partial bid creating cross-currency divergence; oil falling below $85 = inflation fears ease, Oct/Dec hike odds drop and USD bulls face headwinds from both easing oil and softer inflation. End-October compounded vol event: Oct 27-28 FOMC + Oct 29-30 BOJ within 48 hours = maximum USDJPY and JPY-cross volatility. Theme retires: Dec FOMC decision resolves the primary binary; or a 3+ consecutive months of soft CPI/PCE that pushes both Oct and Dec hike odds below 30%.
